title: Vortex solitons in disclination quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye, Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Being structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry $\mathcal{C}_ν$ of order $ν$, photonic quasicrystals are capable to support stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry $ν$ of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states was not investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices were considered in this context. Here we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects -- disclinations -- introduced into their structure that allows to produce new quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We found two different classes of stable vortex solitons consisting of in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, while stability intervals for them broaden with decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry $\mathcal{C}_ν$ of quasicrystal. Our results expand the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting new prospects for robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
summary: This paper explores vortex solitons in quasicrystals by introducing controlled topological defects called disclinations. By modifying the underlying symmetry of the quasicrystal structure, the authors demonstrate the creation of new, stable vortex soliton families. This expands the understanding of wave localization in complex, aperiodically structured photonic media.
main_problem: The study investigates how introducing global topological defects, specifically disclinations, into quasicrystals affects the stable propagation of vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons.
main_result: The introduction of disclinations enriches the linear spectrum, enabling the existence of new, stable, thresholdless vortex solitons whose properties reflect the quasicrystal's discrete rotational symmetry.
method: The analysis uses the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) governing the light field, analyzing the linear spectrum and solving the nonlinear equation numerically.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the quasicrystals are large enough to exhibit the desired symmetries, and the study focuses on the evolution of localized vortex inputs in a pre-fabricated potential.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using the NLSE, details the method of generating defect-laden quasicrystals, analyzes the linear spectrum, and finally presents the findings regarding the bifurcation and stability of vortex solitons.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear optics, topological physics, and quasiperiodicity, showing how engineered defects can fundamentally alter the light-matter interaction and support robust, topologically protected wave states.
